# LEAN_LESSONS — the portable discipline every station carries

owner: stable-kit commons · status: DRAFT for independent check · date: 2026-10-16 · source: lettuce repo (read-only) at its checked-out HEAD · audit: the acceptance tests in § COMMONS ARTIFACTS

**What this is.** The lettuce repo spent two months paying for its own mistakes and writing each one down with the
mechanism that stops it recurring. This file keeps the part of that which has nothing to do with trading or Pine, in a
form a standalone station (a private repo clone built around one domain: BI consulting, design, research, a side
business, trading) can adopt. Each lesson has seven fields: **id · rule · why · mechanism · cost · class · upstream**.

**How to read the fields.**
- **why** cites the lettuce file that holds the incident or measurement. Paths are lettuce-relative and are evidence,
  not something a station must copy.
- **mechanism** prefers something that runs (hook, setting, script, skill, template) over prose. The lettuce lesson
  behind all of them is L99: *a rule in prose that a tool could enforce is a rule the next session will break*.
- **cost** is the adoption cost to a station: what has to be built, plus what it costs on every turn.
- **class**: `MUST` goes into every station. `SHOULD` goes in by default and may be dropped with a stated reason.
  `DOMAIN(<name>)` goes only into stations of that domain.
- **upstream** says what happens when an upstream repo vendored into the station (its own CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or
  `.claude/`) says something different. There are three values:
  - `NEVER`: no upstream file relaxes this rule anywhere in the station.
  - `SUBTREE`: inside `upstream/<owner~repo>/`, that repo's own convention governs the listed concern (build command,
    code style, test runner, commit format) when the station is working ON that tree.
  - `N/A`: upstream trees cannot touch this.

  § PRECEDENCE explains how a station declares this.

**Baggage excluded on purpose.** Pine, phi-geometry, `bridge/` by name, Scion, ticket shifts, PART Z model-name tiers,
RAT and register numbering, merge trains, Fable-as-orchestrator. Where one of these carried a principle that ports,
the lesson keeps the principle without the name.

---

## A · Context diet: what loads every turn is the scarcest resource

### LL-01 · The hot path has a byte budget, and rule bodies load only when their files are read
- **rule:** The station root `CLAUDE.md` holds headlines, commands and pointers within a fixed byte budget. Each rule's
  full body lives in a path-scoped rule file that loads only when a matching file is read.
- **why:** lettuce capped CLAUDE.md at 25,000 B (R10/RAT-015, cited in `.claude/rules/gates.md` and
  `governance/ownership.md` headers) and moved the bodies of invariants 11–13, the bridge rationale and the audit
  history verbatim into `.claude/rules/{gates,bridge,audit}.md`, each with `paths:` frontmatter. After the RAT-057 diet
  of 2026-10-15, CLAUDE.md measures **10,229 B** (`wc -c CLAUDE.md`, 2026-10-16) and still carries 14 invariants and the
  audit command. `governance/INTENTS.yml` § `repertoire_pathways` records which file loads for which path.
- **mechanism:** a template `CLAUDE.md` with a declared `bytes_budget` in `station.yml`. A `.claude/rules/*.md` file
  per rule body, each with `paths:` frontmatter. Station-audit checks `claudemd_bytes` (MUST_BE_CLEAN) and
  `rule_paths_resolve` (every `paths:` glob matches at least one tracked file, otherwise the rule can never load).
- **cost:** low: one template and two audit checks. It saves bytes on every turn of every session.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER (an upstream CLAUDE.md never sits on the station's hot path; see LL-03)

### LL-02 · The per-turn cost of a skill is its listing line, so route instead of listing
- **rule:** Every skill or saved workflow that the router or a human invokes by name is hidden from the model's
  per-turn listing with `skillOverrides: "user-invocable-only"`. Only skills the model must choose for itself stay
  listed. A name shared by a workflow and a skill must not be overridden, because the override hides the skill too.
- **why:** lettuce `.claude/settings.json` carries 71 `skillOverrides` rows: 56 `user-invocable-only` (saved workflows)
  and 15 `off` (vendored upstream skills such as `ccxt-*` and `review-pr`). The contract and its trap are documented
  in `tools/audit_intents.py` `listing()` (measured on Claude Code 2.1.293; the docs cover skills only).
  **Measured for the stable in this pass:** across the 28 stable clones, `git cat-file --batch` over every
  `HEAD:<dir>/SKILL.md` found **359 SKILL.md files**. 353 had parseable frontmatter, and their `name` plus
  `description` total **127,286 characters**, about 32k tokens at 4 chars/token. The largest are Vibe-Trading
  (91 skills, 20,251 chars), pm-skills (69, 19,314), relaticle (31, 17,592) and impeccable (25, 12,704). Against a
  listing budget of 1% of context, this is an **upper bound**: I did not verify whether the harness truncates long
  descriptions.
- **mechanism:** a `skillOverrides` policy block in the settings template. Station-audit check `listing_budget`
  sums the listed skills' name+description bytes against `station.yml: listing_budget_bytes` (MUST_BE_CLEAN). Check
  `listing_overrides` fails on a workflow with no override row, an override naming nothing, or an override that
  shares a skill's name (MUST_BE_CLEAN, the port of `audit_intents.listing()`).
- **cost:** low: a JSON block and a 60-line check. The payoff grows with every upstream skill pack ingested.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER (an upstream skill pack's wish to be listed does not override the station budget)

### LL-03 · Upstream trees live off every auto-discovered path
- **rule:** Vendored upstream trees go under `upstream/<owner~repo>/`. That path is excluded by `claudeMdExcludes` for
  CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md and `.claude/rules/**`. No upstream `.claude/skills` or `.claude/agents` may
  sit anywhere a session might Read, unless its skills carry `skillOverrides` rows.
- **why:** lettuce `.claude/settings.json` `claudeMdExcludes` lists six `**/vendor/**/...` globs. `governance/INTENTS.yml`
  `repertoire_pathways.vendor_nested` (status **open**) records a measurement from 2026-10-15: one Read of
  `vendor/wilsonfreitas~awesome-quant/README.md` injected no upstream CLAUDE.md text, but it DID list three upstream
  skills (`sprr`, `bprr`, `update-pypi-dates`). A nested `.claude/skills` loads the first time any file in its subtree
  is read, and no directory-level exclude covers it. In the stable, 9 repos ship `.claude-plugin/`. `supabase` ships
  `.claude/settings.json` and `openwiki` ships `.claude/settings.local.json` (from `facts.json` `claude_files`).
- **mechanism:** (a) the settings-template `claudeMdExcludes` covering `**/upstream/**`. (b) An ingest script that
  copies an upstream tree and **renames** its `.claude/` to `_upstream_claude/`. The text stays readable as data but is
  no longer discoverable, and the rename is recorded in `upstream/USAGE.yml`. (c) Station-audit check `vendor_leak`
  (MUST_BE_CLEAN) fails on any `upstream/**/.claude/{skills,agents,commands}`, `upstream/**/.claude/settings*.json`,
  `upstream/**/.mcp.json` or `upstream/**/.claude-plugin/` left un-renamed.
- **cost:** low to build. The rename changes the upstream tree's bytes, so it is recorded as a "what was removed or
  renamed" line, the same way lettuce `vendor/CHECKLIST.md` records removals.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** this lesson IS the precedence mechanism. An upstream file never auto-loads; it is read deliberately
  (§ PRECEDENCE).

### LL-04 · Noun decides the station, verb decides the workflow, only the universal stays account-level
- **rule:** What data a capability touches (its noun) decides which station and environment it lives in. What it does
  (investigate, review, design, hand off) decides a workflow that the router dispatches. Only skills that are truly
  universal stay at account level.
- **why:** the sorting principle given to the operator earlier in this session (task brief). It agrees with lettuce's
  CONNECTOR POLICY (`governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md`: Bisharp, Supabase and Context7 are disconnected FOR LETTUCE ONLY,
  because their nouns are not lettuce's) and with the vendor rule that L2 apps "never sit inside lettuce"
  (`docs/research/2026-10-16_REPO_STABLE/ARCHITECTURE_MAPS.md` layer table).
- **mechanism:** `station.yml: nouns:` (data domains), `connectors_allow:` and `verbs:` (router intents). The
  `deny_connector` hook generalised from lettuce `tools/hooks/deny_connector.sh`, reading the allowlist. A commons
  `verbs/` pack that every station receives as files, not as listed skills.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-05 · Token sinks: batch the fetch, never call blind, recall the owner instead of searching
- **rule:** Fetch deferred tool schemas in one batched `select:` call at the point you know the whole set. Never call a
  deferred tool before its schema is loaded. Answer "what owns X" from the ownership table, not with a repo grep.
  Recall a tool's NAME and JOB from memory; read its NUMBER from the tool.
- **why:** lettuce `.claude/skills/claude-consulting-selflearning/SKILL.md` §7.3 (three token sinks measured on real
  sessions) and §7.4 ("name from memory, number from the tool").
- **mechanism:** three lines in the lean CLAUDE.md template, plus `OWNERSHIP.md` (LL-07) as the recall surface.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

## B · One owner, one truth

### LL-06 · Check whether it exists before building it
- **rule:** Before writing a new tool, skill or library, check the problem index (`SOLUTIONS.md`: our answers plus
  upstream answers, each under a problem tag) and the existing exports.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md "Before you build anything, check whether it exists". `lib_ladder` was built beside
  `lib_lattice`'s types (Efficiency-50 E46). `vendor/USAGE.yml` header: "without that, 47,000 vendored files are
  indistinguishable from no vendored files". Hook row 57 in `tools/hooks/README.md` Table A is `remind_prior_art.py`.
- **mechanism:** `upstream/USAGE.yml`, one entry per tree with `what` (one clause), `when` (the situation, not the
  features), `entry` (the first path to open), `solves` (tags from `TAXONOMY.md`) and `licence`, folded by a generator
  into `SOLUTIONS.md`. A PreToolUse·Write hook `remind_prior_art.py` sends a REPORT (never a deny) when a Write
  creates a new file under `tools/`, `skills/` or `lib/`.
- **cost:** medium: a taxonomy has to be curated per station.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-07 · Every rule and register has exactly one owner, and every other mention is a pointer
- **rule:** One canonical owner per rule. A copy is a defect, because two copies drift. A new rule names the rule it
  retires. Superseded text is kept whole and dated: in the file itself for cold files, and moved to a history file
  for hot-path files.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/ownership.md` (the table plus three rules). CLAUDE.md "No new governance subsection lands
  in CLAUDE.md without naming the one it retires" and "AMEND, NEVER DELETE", AMENDED 2026-10-15: superseded text
  in hot-path files moves verbatim to a history file. `audit_canon.py` gates operator text that must not drift (the
  CANON blocks in `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md`). LEDGER L341 records "one ruling, two owners across branches".
- **mechanism:** an `OWNERSHIP.md` table template (`rule · owner · every other occurrence is`). `<!-- CANON:<id> BEGIN/END -->`
  markers, with station-audit check `canon` (MUST_BE_CLEAN) failing when two un-pointered copies of one block exist or
  a quoted block drifts. A `HISTORY.md` file as the destination for superseded hot-path text.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER for station rules. SUBTREE for an upstream's own internal docs, which the station never edits.

### LL-08 · Upstream code is kept verbatim, attributed, off the dependency graph, and only ported from
- **rule:** Copy upstream in unmodified, with its LICENSE in place. Nothing the station ships imports from it. Fix
  upstream or fork under the station's own name with the lineage recorded. Record every removal. "Do not edit these
  files."
- **why:** lettuce `vendor/README.md` ("Nothing in this directory is on the DAG", "Do not edit these files", the
  removals summary). CLAUDE.md: "`vendor/` is port-FROM only".
- **mechanism:** a PreToolUse hook `deny_upstream_write.py` (DENY on Edit/Write/redirect into `upstream/**` except
  `upstream/<tree>/_PATCHES/` labelled `NOT APPLIED`; generalised from `deny_bridge_write.py`'s patches-dir pattern).
  Station-audit check `upstream_index` (MUST_BE_CLEAN, port of `audit_taxonomy.py`) fails when a tree on disk is
  undocumented, a documented tree is missing, an `entry:` path does not resolve, or a LICENSE file is absent.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** SUBTREE: the upstream's own rules govern any upstream PR the operator chooses to make, outside the station.

### LL-09 · Licence is decided before ingest, and copyleft is run as a tool, never vendored into a private product
- **rule:** A GPL or AGPL tree is not copied into a station whose output is proprietary. Use it unvendored, as an
  installed tool or a separate app reached over MCP or HTTP. Read its method and re-implement from that. A permissive
  tree carries its LICENSE with it.
- **why:** lettuce `vendor/README.md` "The 13 that were not lifted": 12 copyleft plus 1 non-commercial, with three
  honest paths, of which path 3 ("use them without vendoring") is "the right answer and costs nothing" for most.
  **In the stable** (`facts.json` `license`), six repos are copyleft: FinceptTerminal (AGPL), erpnext (GPL), lago
  (AGPL), maxun (AGPL), plane (AGPL) and relaticle (AGPL). All six are L2 apps or tools, which is exactly path 3's
  case.
- **mechanism:** a `licence:` field in `upstream/USAGE.yml` plus station-audit check `licence_filter`
  (MUST_BE_CLEAN): fail when a tree whose LICENSE matches `GNU (AFFERO )?GENERAL PUBLIC` sits under `upstream/` in a
  station whose `station.yml: distribution` is `proprietary`. Copyleft apps are listed under `station.yml: services:`
  (run, not vendored).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-10 · A list of what to protect is itself a claim: the protected file and its list entry are one act
- **rule:** Any registry of deploy, protected or audited paths is gated against the tree. Adding the protected file and
  adding its registry entry happen in one commit.
- **why:** lettuce `.claude/rules/audit.md`: `oracle.pine` was live and absent from `DEPLOY`, which "cost four compile
  errors in one sitting… every prior entry on that list was paid for by a compile error first." Table A row 42: a
  CODEOWNERS row naming a path that no longer exists.
- **mechanism:** station-audit check `paths` (MUST_BE_CLEAN): every path named in `station.yml`, CODEOWNERS, router
  `path_patterns`, rule `paths:` and `USAGE.yml entry:` resolves.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

## C · Rules become mechanisms

### LL-11 · A rule a tool can enforce becomes a hook, and every rule records whether it is hooked
- **rule:** For each rule and each failure row, record `hook: HOOKED <script> | OWED <shape> — trigger: … | NOT HOOKABLE <why>`.
  A rule that needs judgement is NOT HOOKABLE; that is a finding, not a gap.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L99 (three session-limit strikes in one afternoon, each a rule already written in a file the
  session could read). `tools/hooks/README.md` Tables A/B: 67 shapes mapped, all L and S rows classed, "the majority
  being NOT HOOKABLE is the finding rather than the gap".
- **mechanism:** a `hook:` line required in every `LEDGER.md` row (template). Station-audit check `hooks_ledger`
  (MUST_BE_CLEAN) fails on a row with no `hook:` line, or a `HOOKED` row naming a script that does not exist or is not
  wired in `settings.json`.
- **cost:** low per row.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-12 · The hook contract: deterministic, self-testing, one line, and only certainty may block
- **rule:** A hook reads the harness JSON on stdin, is deterministic, and carries `--selftest` that plants the shape and
  asserts the exit code. A DENY prints one line to stderr and exits 2. A heuristic never blocks; it WARNs. Matching
  is done on commands at statement boundaries (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, newline, subshell) after stripping heredoc bodies
  and quoted strings. No `if:` permission filter goes on a deny path, because `Bash(git *)` does not match
  `cd x && git add -A`.
- **why:** lettuce `tools/hooks/README.md` "What a hook here may and may not be" and "Why the two masking rules exist".
  **Observed live in this pass:** lettuce's heuristic `warn_vacuous_verify.py` (shape C, register range) fired twice
  on register-range text inside my own `echo` beat lines. That is a false positive, and it cost nothing only because
  the shape is a WARN.
- **mechanism:** a commons `hooks/_cmdscan.py` (strip heredocs and quotes, split at statement boundaries) and a hook
  skeleton with `--selftest`. Station-audit check `hooks_selftest` runs every hook's selftest (MUST_BE_CLEAN).
- **cost:** medium once, in the commons. Each hook after that is about 50 lines.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-13 · A hook's output channel decides who hears it
- **rule:** Plain stdout with exit 0 reaches the model only on SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit (plus
  UserPromptExpansion and PostModelSwitch). On PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SubagentStop it goes to the debug log.
  Reports therefore go through one helper: JSON `additionalContext` for the model, `systemMessage` for the human. Each
  finding is said once per session. A SessionStart readback stays under the 10,000-character preview cap, with a
  declared byte budget.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L335 and `tools/hooks/README.md` AMENDED 2026-09-28 ("Nothing is silent" was false for every
  WARN and REPORT; 11 reporters repeated one text on more than half their runs). Table A rows 13, 27 and 47.
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/_report.py` (who-must-act routing, plus once-per-session dedup keyed by session id).
  Station-audit check `hook_channels` (MUST_BE_CLEAN): every hook wired on a non-delivering event either imports
  `_report` or writes no plain stdout, and every SessionStart reader declares `# budget: <n> B` with `n < 10000`.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-14 · Every deny, pause or latch releases on something the denied act cannot itself require
- **rule:** For every gate, ask what clears it, whether the gate itself can prevent that, and how often the clearing
  condition actually occurs. A gate whose only release is the act it blocks is STUCK, which is worse than silent.
- **why:** lettuce invariants 12–13 (`.claude/rules/gates.md`: a breaker that resets only on the next closed trade
  never resets, and a latch rebuilt every bar is a passthrough). The same shape in the agent layer: Table A row 4,
  where `deny_generated_edit` refused `git checkout --ours <generated>`, the documented repair. "That is a STUCK gate"
  was fixed with a restore-from-record exemption. Rule 25 releases a pause on `.released`, a scoped row, or 24 h.
- **mechanism:** a required `release:` field in every hook's docstring header, checked by station-audit
  `hook_release` (WORKLIST: presence only, because a release path is judgement and LL-12 forbids blocking on
  judgement). The hook skeleton carries a release-path selftest case.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-15 · Stop twice, pause
- **rule:** When one target (a script with its args, or a background task) has stopped twice in 24 h (interrupted,
  timed out or killed), the same session's third launch of it is denied. Report what stopped and why, and take another
  route. Stops count per session.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 25 (the full audit and `pf_deep` were relaunched session after
  session for about 12 h on 2026-10-09: "the sudden total paralysis this repo is facing"), AMENDED 2026-10-15 so stops
  are scoped per session. Table A row 66.
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/stop_twice.py` (PostToolUseFailure/TaskStop recorder → `.station/pause/STOPS.jsonl`;
  PreToolUse deny on the third launch; release via `.station/pause/<target>.released` or 24 h).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-16 · A human's exception is a committed row quoting the human, never an env var
- **rule:** A deny hook releases for an operator exception only through a committed row (`scope`, verbatim `quote`,
  where it was said, `utc`, `expires`). A harness environment variable is never a release.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 25 item 3, and Rules 22–23: authority is cited with its
  locator (session id, event uuid, exact UTC), because two rulings cited as "~12:47Z" were typed at other times and
  three unsourced clauses throttled dispatch for about 25 h.
- **mechanism:** `RELEASES.yml` schema in the commons. A `_release.py` helper that every deny hook calls.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-17 · Destructive shell shapes are denied mechanically
- **rule:** Deny `git add -A`/`.`/`--all` and `commit -a` while another worker holds claims. Deny kill-by-pattern
  (`pkill`, `killall`). Deny force-push to shared branches, `reset --hard`, `clean -f` and `checkout -f` over
  uncommitted work, and `branch -D` of an unmerged tip.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L86 (`git add -A` swept two workers' in-flight files into an unrelated commit; `pkill -f`
  killed a sibling's baseline run), L82, S15/S79, and Table A rows 1, 2 and 11.
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/deny_destructive.py` (one script, the cmdscan from LL-12, a selftest per shape).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-18 · Anything that touches a live process or real money is written as a patch, never in place
- **rule:** A station with a live surface (a trading bridge, a client ERP write endpoint, a production DB, a scheduled
  job that sends mail) never edits that surface directly. Proposed changes go to `<surface>/patches/` with
  `NOT APPLIED` on line 1, and land in a later sweep under explicit per-session authorisation. Reading is always
  allowed.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md "NEVER WRITE INTO `bridge/`", with the rationale in `.claude/rules/bridge.md`: "A bridge
  file edited under a running process costs a POSITION… There is no audit check that can catch this… the damage
  happens outside the repository". Hook `deny_bridge_write.py` (Table A row 3).
- **mechanism:** `station.yml: live_surfaces: [<glob>]`. The commons hook `deny_live_write.py` reads that list (the
  generalisation of `deny_bridge_write.py`) with a `patches/` carve-out.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD (it becomes MUST the moment `live_surfaces` is non-empty)
- **upstream:** NEVER

## D · Routing: the first move is a gather, not a guess

### LL-19 · An intent router injects the mandatory first move on every prompt
- **rule:** A UserPromptSubmit hook classifies each human prompt into one intent from a YAML registry (keywords,
  phrases, path patterns, file types, regexes) and injects that intent's first move (a workflow or skill name plus
  args). It never blocks, and a conversational prompt injects nothing.
- **why:** lettuce `tools/hooks/intent_router.py` docstring (R105: "THERE SHOULD BE NO QUESTION… THAT DOES NOT HAVE A
  SLICE OR HOOK PATH… THE FIRST SHOULD ALWAYS GATHER"). `governance/INTENTS.yml` holds the router rule table. Table A
  row 29.
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/intent_router.py` plus `router/INTENTS.yml`, with the schema in § COMMONS. Design
  constraints carried over from the lettuce docstring, each earned by a measured misroute:
  - It never exits non-zero. Any failure prints one line and exits 0.
  - **Harness turns are not prompts.** A prompt opening with `<task-notification>`, `<agent-message`,
    `another claude session sent a message:`, `<wake reason=`, `<webhook-payload` or `<child-session-event` injects
    nothing. About 15 such turns were misrouted in one session.
  - **A prohibition is not a request.** A hit is cancelled when a negator stands within 3 words before it in the same
    clause. Four words cancelled "no idea why the bridge fails".
  - **The tie rule has one owner in the YAML.** Ties go to the intent whose missed gather costs most if skipped, not
    the one that is cheapest to run.
  - **A multi-intent cap.** A prompt matching N or more intents routes to nothing: 11 of 13 such prompts were pasted
    documents, and the top intent won 7 of 17 ties and all 7 were wrong.
  - Output is at most 1,200 B. Whether the target exists is read from disk at runtime, never hard-coded.
- **cost:** medium once (commons). Each station only writes its `INTENTS.yml`.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER for the router. Upstream skill packs are ROUTED TO by name. They never add router rules of their
  own.

### LL-20 · Running an instrument inline, outside its workflow, is named back to the workflow
- **rule:** When a session runs a station instrument or reads raw data outside its routed workflow, a hook WARNs and
  names the workflow. Lettuce denies at its orchestrator tier; a station without tiers WARNs.
- **why:** lettuce Table A row 31 (`warn_inline_instrument.py`, R110: the classifier half is the router and this is
  the enforcement half).
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/warn_inline_instrument.py`, reading `INTENTS.yml` and honouring a `STATION_WORKFLOW`
  env var that workflow agents set.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

## E · The audit: one command, one exit code, no misreadable green

### LL-21 · One audit with two classes: must-be-clean claims and worklists
- **rule:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py` runs every check and returns one exit code. Each check is classed exactly
  once: **MUST_BE_CLEAN** (a failure means the station asserts something untrue, with no backlog behind it) or
  **WORKLIST** (a counted backlog being driven down, which may also carry a hard sub-gate, the way `lint` gates the
  deploy path at 0 while counting the corpus). The two lists are themselves gated against the prose that names them.
  Run the audit at session start and before every commit.
- **why:** lettuce `tools/audit_all.py` `MUST_BE_CLEAN` (24) and `WORKLISTS` (21), with `audit_canon` gating both tuples
  against CLAUDE.md's two lists. Its `HOSTED_OFF` dict gives each exclusion from the hosted gate a measured reason.
  CLAUDE.md "Run the audit — first thing, and again before you commit".
- **mechanism:** commons `tools/station_audit.py` with a `CHECKS` table, the two tuples, `--state` (a cached one-line
  readback for SessionStart, at most 1,000 B), `--changed` (re-run only checks whose inputs moved) and `-k <check>`.
- **cost:** medium once.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER (upstream test suites may run as checks of their own; they never replace this one)

### LL-22 · A green must never be misreadable
- **rule:** A scraper that cannot read its tool's output returns `UNREADABLE` and fails. It never defaults to green. A
  filtered run says "N/M green (filter …); the rest were NOT run". Every headline carries its denominator, so a green
  on zero rows reads as `0 rows`. Worklist counts are appended to a trend file and a rise is printed.
- **why:** lettuce `tools/audit_all.py` (`check_lint`'s `UNREADABLE` sentinel; the "filtered green is never read as a
  full-repo green" print; `append_profile_trend`). `.claude/rules/audit.md` on `trace`: "empty is green with the
  headline carrying the denominator so a green on zero rows is never misread". Invariant 11: "a gate that silently
  suppresses… is indistinguishable from a signal that never fires".
- **mechanism:** built into the `station_audit.py` skeleton. Each check returns `(ok, headline_with_counts, detail)`.
- **cost:** nil once built.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-23 · A check or hook is admitted only with the defect that earned it
- **rule:** A new check or hook ships with (1) the defect that earned it, in its docstring, (2) a planted-defect
  selftest, (3) its class (MUST_BE_CLEAN or WORKLIST, DENY or WARN or REPORT), and (4) what it retires, or why nothing
  overlaps.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md "Admission rule (RAT-057)". `.claude/rules/audit.md`, where every check's paragraph names
  "the defect that earned it".
- **mechanism:** station-audit check `admission` (MUST_BE_CLEAN) parses every check and hook docstring for
  `earned-by:`, `selftest:`, `class:` and `retires:`.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-24 · Generated files are claims: regenerate before commit, never hand-edit, rebuild after combining
- **rule:** A generated file carries a banner naming its generator. Hand edits of it are denied, except a restore from
  a recorded source (`--ours`/`--theirs`/`<rev> -- <path>`). It is regenerated before every commit. Any tool that
  combines N inputs (a merge of branches) rebuilds every derived file from the combination before judging it. A
  worker rule that forbids running the generator makes the worker's output red by construction.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md "A generated file in git is a CLAIM: regenerate before you commit". Table A row 4
  (`deny_generated_edit.py` with its restore exemption). LEDGER L409 (three clean branch tips merged into a red
  catalog/README). L196 (13 of 37 red CI runs came from a lane forbidden to run the generators).
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/deny_generated_edit.py` (banner in the first 3 lines). `make generate` as the single
  entry point. Station-audit check `generated_fresh` (MUST_BE_CLEAN) re-renders each generated file to a temp path and
  diffs it.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** SUBTREE (an upstream's own generated files follow its own generator, and the station never regenerates
  them)

### LL-25 · A certain test must be able to fail, and its author runs it once before issuing it
- **rule:** Every workflow, skill or delegated task names one command whose exit code settles success. `test -e <file>`
  is not a certain test. The author runs it once against the real tree before issuing it. Workflow stages inject
  live facts (command output) rather than prose plus the prior stage's self-report.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L275 (of 57 workflow `certain_test` rows, 31 could not fail by their shape, 20 of them being
  `test -e`, and 10 could not run as written). L279 (0 exec/read calls in 51 workflow scripts; "a stage told to run
  audit_gates and list could skip the run, and nothing would notice"). L120 (a spec wording whose own certain test the
  author never ran). `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 4: "If a task cannot be clearly tested, redefine it until it
  can, then delegate."
- **mechanism:** station-audit check `certain_tests` (MUST_BE_CLEAN, port of `audit_intents --probe`), which flags
  DRIFT, NO-TOOL, NO-VERB, CANNOT-RUN, MUTATES and existence-only. Skills inject live state with the `` !`cmd` ``
  dynamic-context syntax, the way lettuce `handoff/SKILL.md` and `claude-consulting-selflearning/SKILL.md` open with
  `` !`python3 tools/audit_all.py --state` `` and `` !`git log --oneline -8` ``.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-26 · Hosted CI is minimal; the full audit runs locally
- **rule:** Hosted CI runs only the fast must-be-clean subset on pull requests, with a minutes budget. The full audit
  and the slow real-data checks run locally or nightly.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` "Hosted CI retired as a gate": about 300 hosted runs of about 7 min
  each exhausted the month's minutes, and the operator said "it has literally never caught anything that isn't just
  infrastructure". AMENDED 2026-10-15: one minimal `gate.yml` (MUST_BE_CLEAN minus `HOSTED_OFF`, an 8-minute cap,
  a 2,000-minute monthly budget).
- **mechanism:** a `gate.yml` template running `station_audit.py --gate --affected origin/main`, plus `HOSTED_OFF`
  with a measured reason per row.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** SUBTREE (an upstream's own CI is irrelevant to the station and never runs)

## F · Epistemics: a claim is evidence only once it is re-derived

### LL-27 · Re-derive an inherited claim before building on it, a negative claim most of all
- **rule:** Before acting on "tool X is broken, missing or lying", run X and read its own summary. A negative claim in a
  handoff is re-derived in the session that writes it.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L1, the most-cited row in governance, tools and skills (97 citations;
  `grep -rhoE "\bL[0-9]{1,3}\b" CLAUDE.md .claude governance tools/hooks/README.md tools/*.py | sort | uniq -c`).
  A false "silently truncated" claim passed four authors deep and ordered a whole plan, and one command disproved it.
  `handoff/SKILL.md` §3.1: "an absence looks identical whether you looked carefully or not at all".
- **mechanism:** gate 1 in the close-out skill. A `negative-claims:` field in the handoff template whose entries each
  carry the command that was run.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-28 · Read the instrument's whole output once; run slow tools once, capture, grep the file
- **rule:** Before grepping a tool's output, read all of it once, because the summary lines answer the question you
  should have asked. Run a slow tool once, save its output to a file, then grep the file. Never chain several slow
  invocations in one command.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L2 (a truncated listing was grepped and the tool was blamed: "a measurement taken with the
  wrong instrument reads exactly like a defect in the instrument"). L7 (four slow runs chained into one command hit
  the 2-minute timeout and lost the turn).
- **mechanism:** gates 2 and 7 in the close-out skill. A `run_once.sh <name> -- <cmd>` helper that tees to
  `.station/cache/<name>.txt`.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-29 · Name from memory, number from the tool: never transcribe a counter
- **rule:** A document cites the COMMAND (`audit: python3 tools/station_audit.py`), not its reading (`15/15 green`). A
  number that must appear in prose carries its date and the command that produced it. A checkpoint is a register.
  Hand-typed IDs come from an allocator.
- **why:** lettuce `handoff/SKILL.md` §3.2. LEDGER L66 (a plot budget counted by eye was wrong by exactly the two calls
  the counter did not know about). L87 (an agent's figure was transcribed into the plan and a checkpoint without being
  re-derived). Table A row 8 (`check_checkpoint.py`: a number with no command behind it). `.claude/rules/audit.md`
  `registers` (two sessions numbering forward from one merge base produced 44 ID collisions).
- **mechanism:** station-audit check `checkpoints` (MUST_BE_CLEAN): every number in a checkpoint sits next to a command
  or a resolvable commit hash. A `tools/alloc_id.py` that reads the shared ref's maximum for any station register.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-30 · Anchors are text, never line numbers
- **rule:** Cite `function_name`'s trail or a section heading, not `file.py:4738`.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L13 (the plan's own line-number anchors were stale when anyone followed them).
  `audit_handoff.py` flags every `path.ext:NNN`.
- **mechanism:** a station-audit check `anchors` (WORKLIST) over handoffs and checkpoints.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-31 · A defect found and only written down is a defect shipped
- **rule:** On finding a real defect, either fix it, or register it in its owning register with a re-test trigger in
  the same pass, and say in one sentence which of the two happened. "Noted" is not an outcome. A defect in a file your
  own lane wrote or must regenerate is never "out of scope".
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Invariant 14 ("thats like me writing damn that sql is rough af and
  then doing nothing"), AMENDED 2026-10-09: a child lane left its own TRI_ASC/TRI_DSC defect as "out of scope". Table A
  row 64 (`deny_noted_defect.py` denies hedging words with no register id).
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/deny_noted_defect.py` (staged lines in report files matching
  `noted|pre-existing|not mine|for the next author` with no register id → DENY). A return-schema field
  `left: [{kind, owner, trigger}]` validated by `check_return.py`, which rejects `own-defect-left`.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-32 · Every gate reports, including every refusal, skip and null
- **rule:** Anything that can refuse, skip or drop must reach something the human sees. Report refused, aborted and
  null agents as well as successful ones. A silently shortened result set reads as complete coverage.
- **why:** lettuce invariant 11 (`.claude/rules/gates.md`: SILENT / STUCK / DEAD as three distinct pathologies).
  `summon/SKILL.md` §S7 ("a fan-out reported only by its survivors is the suppressed-signal defect") and P7 NULL
  ("`.filter(Boolean)` and say what was dropped").
- **mechanism:** in the summon-lite report template and the `station_audit.py` skeleton.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-33 · Own-rule, interface and premise-before-approval gates
- **rule:**
  1. Re-read any rule written this session before committing, because writing it feels like having followed it.
  2. A change to a tool's flags or output updates its docstring in the same edit.
  3. Verify the premises a decision rests on before putting that decision to the human.
- **why:** lettuce LEDGER L5 (×2, the second time inside the pass that wrote the gate), L3 (two CLI flags shipped
  undocumented in "the tool built to catch stale claims") and L6 (an approval was taken on a premise L1/L2 then
  falsified). `claude-consulting-selflearning/SKILL.md` §2, gates 3, 5 and 6.
- **mechanism:** the gates list in the close-out skill. Station-audit check `cli_doc` (WORKLIST): argparse flags with no
  docstring mention.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

## G · Delegation: the fan-out multiplies every mistake

### LL-34 · The cheapest agent is the one not spawned; N comes from the list; blocks are capped
- **rule:** Spawn only when (1) the work is already enumerated, (2) it is genuinely parallel, and (3) reading the result
  costs less than doing the work. Write the work list first, and set N to the number of independent slices. Concurrency
  is `min(16, nproc − 2)`, measured on the box and never carried as a constant. A block holds at most 4 agents and runs
  about 1 hour, with its budget stated before launch. Depth stays at 2 or less.
- **why:** lettuce `summon/SKILL.md` S0, S1 and M3 (`nproc`=4 gave a cap of 2, the same figure the plan reached by
  measurement). §1, the fan-out multiplier: "a tier error made once costs 1×; across a fan-out it costs N×".
  `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 17 (blocks sized to the cap after "the 8-hour stop" that burned about a third
  of the compute). S37: PRIME exceeded the cap twice in one day. Table A row 32 (`summon_cap_guard.py`).
- **mechanism:** the summon-lite skill (S0 three questions recorded). Commons hook `summon_cap_guard.py` (PreToolUse on
  Agent/Workflow: deny when the block dir holds 4 or more agent artifacts in the window; release when the window
  expires).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-35 · Tier from the work, name model and effort explicitly, raise effort before model
- **rule:** Choose model and effort from what the slice demands. Name both on every slice above the cheapest tier,
  because an omitted model inherits the parent's model. When a slice skipped files or did not run checks, raise the
  EFFORT. When it reasoned wrongly on available information, raise the MODEL. Never raise both at once. Never raise a
  whole fan-out for one hard slice; split that slice out.
- **why:** lettuce `tier/SKILL.md` §1: of 58 procedural failures, **38 were EFFORT and 20 JUDGEMENT** ("not one of the
  thirty-eight would have been fixed by a larger model"). §6 covers the mid-flight correction. `summon/SKILL.md` S2,
  and S47 (a six-agent fan-out ran five slices at the wrong id because the model was omitted).
- **mechanism:** tier-lite skill with six scored dimensions (reversibility, measurement risk, ambiguity, read-breadth,
  novelty, autonomy) and a fixed output shape. Its first rule is "cheapest model that can be checked with certainty".
  Lettuce's model names are baggage; each station keeps a roster in `station.yml`.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-36 · A contract: one deliverable, a certain test, a named refusal, a forbidden list
- **rule:** Every agent is summoned with all of the following:
  - one named deliverable and a result schema
  - its slice, wall-clock bound and beat path
  - its certain test
  - "return null rather than guess; every unknown ends with the test that would settle it, or `no test exists from
    this data`"
  - the forbidden list for its rank, including setting or exporting `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`
    by name
  - if it writes where another tool globs, an output that falls outside that glob by construction (another extension
    or directory), never by a name filter
- **why:** lettuce `summon/SKILL.md` S3 (with the S98 amendment for `GIT_*`). S9: two of four agents filed a field as
  undecidable, one named the discriminator, and the parent ran it in one call and closed the hole. S11/S13: a writer
  put `.csv` into a capture-census directory, and a reader widened its glob onto another tool's guard extension.
  Rule 19: a worker never substitutes its own attribution trailer.
- **mechanism:** a contract template in summon-lite. A return schema with `status`, `deliverable`, `certain_test`
  (command plus its output), `gaps` and `left`. A `check_return.py` validator.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-37 · Heartbeats: file channel, append, a cadence from the measured ceiling
- **rule:** A worker appends (`>>`, never `>`) one beat line every `BEAT_S` to its beat file, giving at least three per
  cadence window. Three changing beats means moving; three identical beats means STUCK; two missed beats means SILENT.
  A beat's time is the time the receiver logged it, not the stamp the worker wrote.
- **why:** lettuce `summon/SKILL.md` §0 M1 (the 600 s observation ceiling was measured twice: "the work never stopped,
  only the watching stopped"). Cadence = 600 − 60 = 540 s, beat = 180 s. S29 and S33 (54 minutes with one beat line;
  the worker had overwritten instead of appending). S4 AMENDED: 11 of 23 beats were stamped LATER than their own
  delivery.
- **mechanism:** a beat-line format in summon-lite (`<utc> <lane> step=<n>/<N> <what changed>`). Stop/SubagentStop hook
  `worktree_state.py` reports a stale beat or a dirty worktree once (Table A rows 6, 7 and 9).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD (MUST for any delegation longer than one cadence)
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-38 · A returned claim is evidence, never a finding
- **rule:** Verify returned claims as follows:
  - Re-run the cited argv and diff its hits against the claim.
  - Count callers with comments stripped before calling anything LIVE, because a docstring is not a caller.
  - An agent's grep is a claim until you run it.
  - Verify a cite list line by line.
  - Reviewers use DIFFERENT lenses (arithmetic, fit, reproduce), because N identical skeptics agreeing is a tautology.
  - A worker's own tool-call count is not a measurement.
- **why:** lettuce `summon/SKILL.md` S6. Its cases:
  - S4: a false docstring was reported as a live mechanism.
  - S7: a "grep returns only its declaration" claim named an identifier absent from the file.
  - S72: re-running the argv overturned 19 of 86 rows.
  - S18: self-reported tool calls ran 45 against 156 measured by the harness.
  - P6 SHARED-ERROR covers same-wave agreement (CLAUDE.md invariant 4, one layer up).
  - Measured on the first run: the review cost more than the build and was the only step that caught a bar on the
    wrong denominator.
- **mechanism:** a verify checklist in summon-lite. A `reverify.py` that re-runs every `certain_test` command in a
  return and compares exit codes.
- **cost:** medium per delegation, and paid only where the claim is load-bearing (LL-39).
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-39 · Probe before infrastructure; scale review to what the artifact can cost; a blocking finding names the harm
- **rule:**
  1. A throwaway probe answers "is there any signal at all" before any harness is built.
  2. Full multi-lens review applies only to a number that reaches a decision. A tool gets a REPRODUCE lens. Prose,
     registers and checkpoints get no reviewer agent; the audit is their reviewer.
  3. Only a finding that names concrete downstream harm may block.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rules 13, 14 and 15 (ratified after the 2026-09-17 "8-hour stop":
  "two agents reading the same prose is redundancy, and redundancy is a defect billed in dollars").
- **mechanism:** a review-scaling table in summon-lite. A `blocking:` field in review returns that requires a `harm:`
  string.
- **cost:** nil. It saves cost.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-40 · Terse traffic, and one line to the human at every block boundary
- **rule:** One line wherever one line suffices. Agent and orchestrator talk in shorthand (`lane · sha · pass/fail ·
  next`). At every block boundary, before anything is filed, the human gets one line: what the product can now do,
  what it cost (agents · tokens · minutes), and the one next step. The orchestrator never opens a side lane on its
  own judgement; it names the lane in that line and waits for the word.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 18 ("Opus is so ridiculously verbose") and Rule 16 ("a mirror
  the operator has not read is not a report").
- **mechanism:** a block-close template in summon-lite. The report line shape from `summon/SKILL.md` §S7
  (`SUMMON <run> n=<N>/<slices> cap=… budget=…` plus one row per agent).
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-41 · Never launder a denial, never route around a hook
- **rule:** Never ask a peer session or a subagent to do what your own session was denied, or what you expect to be
  denied. A worker that hits a hook denial reports it; it never finds another path to the same act.
- **why:** lettuce `cross-session/SKILL.md` "The rule that matters most" (cross-session permission laundering).
  SUMMON_LEDGER S17 (a worker routed around a `deny_generated_edit` denial instead of reporting it).
- **mechanism:** a contract clause in summon-lite. A `denials:` field in the return schema.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-42 · Isolation: one worktree per agent, one writer per path, never force or rebase a shared branch
- **rule:** Each writing agent works in its own worktree on its own branch and returns a branch tip, not a dirty tree.
  A shared file is claimed before it is written. Run `git pull --ff-only` before the first edit and before every
  commit. Commit by path at every closed sub-step.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rule 3 and Supersession 3. `cross-session/SKILL.md` "Shared-branch
  protocol" (two sessions on one branch collided live on three files, and "no check will ever report this").
  `summon/SKILL.md` §S10.1 (a beat line with no commit behind it protects nothing) and pathology P8 COLLISION.
- **mechanism:** summon-lite worktree recipe (`git worktree add .worktrees/<agent> -b wt/<agent> HEAD`). Stop hook
  `worktree_state.py` (LL-37).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-43 · Name the failure precisely: the eight agent pathologies
- **rule:** "The agent failed" is eight different defects with eight different responses: SILENT, STUCK, DRIFT,
  CONFABULATION, OVERSPEND, SHARED-ERROR, NULL and COLLISION. SILENT and OVERSPEND do not announce themselves.
- **why:** lettuce `summon/SKILL.md` §5, named after `GATE_PATHOLOGY.md` for the same reason.
- **mechanism:** a vocabulary table in summon-lite. A `pathology:` field in each ledger row.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

## H · Continuity: the next session starts, it does not orient

### LL-44 · Checkpoint when work becomes durable; compaction and clear reopen on the plan, not the diff
- **rule:** Write a checkpoint after every accepted slice and every commit. It carries the commit hash, the paths
  touched, numbers with their commands, what is owed with its trigger, and the next slice's contract. The plan is the
  source of truth, never the diff. A SessionStart hook on `startup|resume|compact|clear` prints, within a byte budget,
  the plan head, the newest checkpoint's `NEXT` block and `station_audit.py --state`.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` rules 2, 7 and 9 (checkpoint and compaction). Table A rows 14 and 27
  (THE CONTEXT LADDER: a source-aware byte budget, 1,900 B on compact under the ~2 KB preview), row 34 (`/clear`
  opened blind) and row 13 (a 9,000 B cap).
- **mechanism:** commons `hooks/context_ladder.py` with a byte budget per SessionStart source. Checkpoint skill and
  template. Station-audit check `checkpoints` (LL-29).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-45 · The handoff: five header fields, five sections, waves a fresh worker can take alone
- **rule:** The header has `branch`, `date`, `covers`, `supersedes` and `audit: <command>` in the first 40 lines. The
  body has five sections: where things stand, what changed and what it means, what is next as waves (each with
  deliverable, files, tier, done-test and refusal), what is blocked and on whom, and open questions each with what
  would settle it. Corrections go where the reader acts, not into a changelog.
- **why:** lettuce `handoff/SKILL.md` §1–§4 (`covers:` makes more than one current handoff safe, as the real corpus
  showed. L14: corrections in a preamble leave the row a reader acts on still wrong).
- **mechanism:** handoff-lite skill, opening with live context injected by `` !`cmd` ``. Station-audit check `handoff`
  (WORKLIST, port of `audit_handoff.py`: header fields, line-number anchors, transcribed counters).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-46 · Close every pass with one ranked next step and the triggers that are about to fire
- **rule:** A pass ends with `NEXT — <one thing>`, plus `why now`, `tier`, `first act` (a literal command or file) and
  `after it`. Then come the parked items, each with its trigger ("later" is not a trigger), and what a fresh session
  would get wrong from reading only the diff. Check the distance to every live trigger, because a fired trigger with no
  checker behind it is a reminder nobody receives. At a plan-declared tier boundary, write `STOP —` and actually stop.
- **why:** lettuce `claude-consulting-selflearning/SKILL.md` §8 (operator: "I don't see you often as well recommending
  the next step") and §2 gate 9 (LEDGER L11: a tiered plan executed as one uninterrupted run and narrated afterwards).
  `tier/SKILL.md` §1 (the L45 trigger fired and nothing noticed).
- **mechanism:** closeout skill (selflearning-lite) with the NEXT shape. A `triggers.yml` (id, condition command,
  threshold) plus station-audit check `triggers` (WORKLIST: prints the distance to each trigger).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-47 · A procedural-failure ledger that amends mechanisms, not conduct
- **rule:** Every procedural or delegation failure gets a row in the same commit as the work: what happened, what it
  cost, the gate, a `hook:` line (LL-11), and a NAMED amendment that would have mechanically prevented it. "Be more
  careful" is not an amendment. A recurrence is logged under the original row, never as a new one.
- **why:** lettuce `docs/selflearning/LEDGER.md` header ("Never delete a row, supersede it"; its effort/judgement
  split feeds `tier/SKILL.md`). `docs/selflearning/SUMMON_LEDGER.md` and `summon/SKILL.md` S8. LEDGER L401: "the ten
  fixes land as mechanisms, not as conduct".
- **mechanism:** `LEDGER.md` template. Station-audit check `ledger` (MUST_BE_CLEAN: unique ids, a `hook:` line present,
  an `amendment:` that is not empty or "be careful").
- **cost:** low per row.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-48 · Read the human's words first-hand and cite them with a locator
- **rule:** When a session needs the human's ruling, it reads the words itself from the record (a transcript, an issue,
  an event) and cites them verbatim with a locator (session or issue id, event id, exact UTC). It never asks the human
  to relay words that a readable record already holds.
- **why:** lettuce `governance/OPERATOR_RULES.md` Rules 22 and 23 ("you have the capability don't offshore work to me";
  rulings cited as "~12:47Z" were typed at 12:42:52Z).
- **mechanism:** a citation format in the commons `RELEASES.yml` and decision-log templates.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-49 · The session cairn records what was HELD versus what was USED
- **rule:** At session close, record what the session considered and did not build, where each idea came from and
  where it lives now, and what the session cost.
- **why:** lettuce `diary/SKILL.md` §0 and §3.2 (HELD is "the field the whole skill exists for": no other register
  records the road not taken).
- **mechanism:** diary-lite template (optional).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** SHOULD
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-50 · A station's MUST rules cannot depend on anything that does not load where the station runs
- **rule:** MUST-class enforcement lives in the station repo's own `.claude/settings.json` hooks and scripts. It never
  lives only in a plugin or marketplace, which do not load in Claude Code cloud sessions. A station that may run in a
  multi-repo cloud session, which loads no repo's hooks, re-runs its checks through `station_audit.py` at session start
  and before commit.
- **why:** task brief facts: plugins and marketplaces do not load in cloud sessions, and a multi-repo cloud session
  loads no hooks. Lettuce Table A row 59 (`automode_ensure.py`: the classifier never reads `autoMode` from the repo
  settings, so the repo had to re-install it at SessionStart). Row 25: the environment install must run automatically.
- **mechanism:** a `bootstrap.sh` invoked by a SessionStart hook (idempotent `--ensure`). The station audit doubles as
  the enforcement floor when hooks are absent.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-51 · Every number carries its denominator
- **rule:** A reported rate, total or verdict states its n, the population it came from, and the command that produced
  it. A green on zero rows prints `0`.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md prime directive (RAT-052: "NO NUMERATOR EVER NOT HAVE ITS DENOMINATOR").
  `quant/harness/MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT.md` is cited by CLAUDE.md "Record the denominator". `summon/SKILL.md` §0 ("every
  number below is a measurement with a stated denominator"). The portable core is that a numerator without its
  denominator cannot be checked. The trading form is LL-D1.
- **mechanism:** station-audit headline convention (LL-22). A `denominator:` field in every return schema that reports
  a count.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** MUST
- **upstream:** N/A

---

## I · DOMAIN lessons

### LL-D1 · A forward claim carries its n, interval and out-of-sample walk, and never weights the window it was measured on
- **rule:** An expected-return or edge claim is stated as a forward claim only with its n, its interval and an
  out-of-sample walk-forward. No weight uses an estimate measured on the same window (the LEAK rule). Weights shrink
  by n.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md prime directive (RAT-052, `governance/RATIFICATIONS.md` Range T). Selflearning gate 10
  AMENDED 2026-10-05: FIT refutes a claim missing its denominator or OOS walk, or one that breaks LEAK.
- **mechanism:** a measurement-contract template, a preregistration register (P-rows) and a review FIT lens.
- **cost:** medium.
- **class:** DOMAIN(trading)
- **upstream:** NEVER (an upstream backtest framework's own reporting does not satisfy this)

### LL-D2 · Honest bands and independent evidence
- **rule:**
  - Never call an empirical band Gaussian, and keep state bands distinct from predictive bands.
  - Agreement between two views on the same data is a tautology; confluence needs different inputs.
  - Each evidence family gets at most one weighted vote.
  - In-sample or undenominated advisory output never arms a decision.
  - The forming bar is provisional.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md invariants 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9.
- **mechanism:** review FIT lens checklist (trading pack).
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** DOMAIN(trading). The "agreement in one wave is a tautology" half is portable and is already MUST through
  LL-38.
- **upstream:** NEVER

### LL-D3 · Never lose a falsification
- **rule:** A refuted idea reaches the negative-results register, with its re-test condition, in the commit that
  establishes it. A new attempt checks that register first.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md "never lose a falsification (`quant/NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md`)". LEDGER L4 (a falsification
  preserved in the wrong file was undiscoverable). Selflearning gate 4.
- **mechanism:** `NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md` template with a `retest:` field. The router's `edge`/`research` intent reads it
  as its first gather.
- **cost:** low.
- **class:** DOMAIN(trading, research). For other stations it is SHOULD under the name "decisions we tried and
  reversed".
- **upstream:** N/A

### LL-D4 · Analysis never draws; every drawn object has a delete-on-redraw path
- **rule:** Computation and presentation are separate units. Anything a renderer creates has a deletion path on
  redraw.
- **why:** lettuce CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (Pine-specific in its wording).
- **mechanism:** none portable beyond review. It is stated here so a design or BI station can choose to adopt the
  principle.
- **cost:** nil.
- **class:** DOMAIN(trading). A BI or design analogue is NOT established from this data (see gaps).
- **upstream:** SUBTREE (an upstream dashboard or chart library follows its own render model)

**BI / consulting domain.** The lettuce sources hold no BI-specific rule (Qlik, ERP, client data). LL-51 (denominators),
LL-18 (live client surfaces are patched, never edited in place), LL-04 (the connector allowlist puts the client-data MCP
in the BI station only) and LL-09 (licence) all apply, but no BI DOMAIN row is derived here. Inventing one would break
LL-27.

---

## PRECEDENCE — how a station states which rules govern upstream subtrees

Upstream text is DATA, not instructions. A station never follows an upstream CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or skill. It
describes what the upstream asks, decides what to adopt, and records that decision. The station declares precedence in
one file, `upstream/PRECEDENCE.yml`, which the station CLAUDE.md points to in a single line:

```yaml
# upstream/PRECEDENCE.yml — one row per vendored tree; read by station_audit `precedence` (MUST_BE_CLEAN)
default: station        # station MUST rules bind everywhere, including inside upstream/**
trees:
  - path: upstream/<owner~repo>/
    licence: MIT                      # from the tree's LICENSE; GPL/AGPL here fails licence_filter
    agent_files_found: [CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/skills/x]   # as found at ingest, by git ls-tree
    agent_files_renamed_to: _upstream_claude/                      # LL-03: off every auto-discovered path
    loaded: never-auto                # claudeMdExcludes + rename; read only on purpose
    governs: [build, code-style, test-runner]                      # SUBTREE concerns only
    summary_of_upstream_asks: "uses pnpm; tests via vitest; conventional commits"  # paraphrase, never import
    adopted: [test-runner]            # what the station actually honours when editing a fork of this tree
```

Rules for the file:
- `governs:` may name only SUBTREE concerns: build, style, test runner, commit format and file layout inside that
  tree. Any lesson classed `upstream: NEVER` above cannot be named there, and the `precedence` check fails if one is.
- Paraphrase only. No upstream sentence addressed to an agent is copied into a station instruction file. A sentence
  kept for the record goes under `upstream/<tree>/_upstream_claude/` as data.
- When the station's own CLAUDE.md conflicts with an upstream convention outside `governs:`, the station wins and
  nothing needs to be said. Inside `governs:`, the upstream convention wins for edits to that tree only.

## COMMONS ARTIFACTS TO BUILD

Each artifact lists **name · kind · path · purpose · implements · acceptance**. Paths are relative to a station root.
The commons core ships every artifact below. A station adds only its `station.yml`, `router/INTENTS.yml`,
`TAXONOMY.md`, `upstream/` and domain pack.

### CA-01 · station.yml
- **kind:** config (YAML), the single source of station constants
- **path:** `station.yml`
- **purpose:** It holds the station's own values, so no hook or check hard-codes a number:
  - `name`, `nouns`, `verbs`, `distribution` (proprietary / open)
  - `connectors_allow`, `live_surfaces`, `services` (run-not-vendored apps)
  - `bytes_budget` (CLAUDE.md), `listing_budget_bytes`, `sessionstart_budget_bytes`
  - `beat_s`, `cadence_s`, `block_max_agents`, `model_roster`
- **implements:** LL-01, LL-02, LL-04, LL-09, LL-18, LL-34, LL-37
- **acceptance:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py -k station_yml` exits 0. It validates the file against
  `commons/schema/station.schema.json`, and its selftest fails on a planted missing key.

### CA-02 · Lean CLAUDE.md template
- **kind:** template (Markdown)
- **path:** `CLAUDE.md`
- **purpose:** The hot path, in this order:
  - the one-line station purpose and the noun/verb boundary
  - the audit command and the start/commit rule
  - MUST invariants, as headlines only, each pointing to its owner
  - the context-diet rule ("bodies live in `.claude/rules/`; superseded hot-path text moves to `HISTORY.md`")
  - a one-line pointer to `upstream/PRECEDENCE.yml`
  - the token-sink lines (LL-05)

  It contains no rule body that `OWNERSHIP.md` assigns elsewhere.
- **implements:** LL-01, LL-05, LL-07, LL-21, PRECEDENCE
- **acceptance:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py -k claudemd_bytes -k canon` exits 0. `claudemd_bytes` fails on a
  planted file over `bytes_budget`. Lettuce's post-diet file measures 10,229 B. A fresh station's budget is a choice
  until measured (see gaps).

### CA-03 · settings.json template
- **kind:** config (JSON)
- **path:** `.claude/settings.json`
- **purpose:**
  - `claudeMdExcludes` for `**/upstream/**/{CLAUDE.md,CLAUDE.local.md,AGENTS.md}`, `**/upstream/**/.claude/**` and
    `**/_upstream_claude/**`
  - a `skillOverrides` policy, `user-invocable-only` for every routed workflow and verb pack
  - the hook wiring for CA-05 to CA-14, each command guarded with `cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" || exit 0`
  - a read-only `permissions.allow` baseline
- **implements:** LL-02, LL-03, LL-12, LL-13, LL-50
- **acceptance:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py -k hooks_wired -k listing_overrides -k vendor_leak` exits 0.
  `hooks_wired` fails on a wired command whose script is missing and on a hook script wired nowhere (a planted orphan).

### CA-04 · OWNERSHIP.md, HISTORY.md and LEDGER.md templates
- **kind:** templates (Markdown)
- **path:** `governance/OWNERSHIP.md`, `governance/HISTORY.md`, `governance/LEDGER.md`
- **purpose:**
  - OWNERSHIP: the one-owner table.
  - HISTORY: the verbatim destination for superseded hot-path text.
  - LEDGER: procedural and delegation failure rows with `hook:`, `amendment:` and `pathology:`.
- **implements:** LL-07, LL-11, LL-43, LL-47
- **acceptance:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py -k canon -k ledger -k hooks_ledger` exits 0. `ledger` fails on a
  planted row with `amendment: be more careful` and on a duplicate id.

### CA-05 · hooks/_cmdscan.py, hooks/_report.py and hooks/_release.py
- **kind:** hook library (Python, stdlib only)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/_cmdscan.py`, `.claude/hooks/_report.py`, `.claude/hooks/_release.py`
- **purpose:**
  - `_cmdscan`: strip heredocs and quotes, then split at statement boundaries.
  - `_report`: route a finding to `additionalContext` (model) or `systemMessage` (human), once per session per finding.
  - `_release`: read `RELEASES.yml` rows (scope, quote, locator, utc, expires).
- **implements:** LL-12, LL-13, LL-16
- **acceptance:** `python3 .claude/hooks/_cmdscan.py --selftest && python3 .claude/hooks/_report.py --selftest` exits
  0. The cmdscan selftest must pass `echo "git add -A"` (inside quotes) and must flag `cd x && git add -A`.

### CA-06 · hooks/intent_router.py and router/INTENTS.yml schema
- **kind:** hook (UserPromptSubmit) plus registry (YAML)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/intent_router.py`, `router/INTENTS.yml`, `commons/schema/intents.schema.json`
- **purpose:** classify each human prompt and inject the mandatory first move. Schema:
  ```yaml
  intents:
    - name: <id>
      description: <one clause>
      router:
        keywords: [..]           # frozen before selftest prompts are written; never widened to fit one
        phrases: [..]
        path_patterns: [..]
        file_types: [..]
        patterns: [..]           # optional regexes over the lowercased prompt
        first_move: {workflow|skill: <name>, args: "<what to pass>", inline_gather: "<fallback>"}
  router_tie_rule:
    order: [<most costly-if-skipped first>, ..., conversational]
    reason: <why, by cost-if-skipped>
    multi_intent_cap: <n>
  harness_prefixes: [...]        # the turn openers that are not human prompts
  negators: [no, never, "don't", "do not", ...]
  neg_window: 3
  ```
- **implements:** LL-04, LL-19
- **acceptance:** `python3 .claude/hooks/intent_router.py --selftest` exits 0 over at least 30 fixture prompts. The
  fixtures include a harness-prefixed turn (empty output), "Never write <live surface>." (no route), "no idea why X
  fails" (routes), a 3-intent pasted document (no route), and an output of 1,200 B or less on every case.
  `station_audit -k router_targets` fails when a `first_move` names a workflow or skill that does not exist on disk.

### CA-07 · hooks/deny_destructive.py
- **kind:** hook (PreToolUse·Bash, DENY)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/deny_destructive.py`
- **purpose:** deny `git add -A`/`.`/`--all` and `commit -a`, kill-by-pattern, force-push to shared branches,
  `reset --hard`/`clean -f`/`checkout -f` over uncommitted work, and `branch -D` of an unmerged tip.
- **implements:** LL-17, LL-14 (its release is that the act is legitimate under its exact named form, e.g.
  `git add <paths>`)
- **acceptance:** `python3 .claude/hooks/deny_destructive.py --selftest` exits 0. Each shape is planted (expect exit 2
  and one stderr line), each allowed sibling is planted (`kill <pid>`, `git add path`, expect exit 0), and a quoted
  mention is planted (exit 0).

### CA-08 · hooks/deny_generated_edit.py
- **kind:** hook (PreToolUse·Bash|Edit|Write, DENY)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/deny_generated_edit.py`
- **purpose:** deny hand edits of any file whose first 3 lines carry `GENERATED by <tool>`. Exempt restores from a
  recorded source (`--ours`, `--theirs`, `--source=<rev>`, `<rev> -- <path>`).
- **implements:** LL-24, LL-14
- **acceptance:** the selftest exits 0, with Edit of a bannered file giving 2, `git checkout --ours <gen>` giving 0, and
  `git checkout -- <gen>` giving 2.

### CA-09 · hooks/deny_upstream_write.py and hooks/deny_live_write.py
- **kind:** hooks (PreToolUse·Bash|Edit|Write, DENY)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/deny_upstream_write.py`, `.claude/hooks/deny_live_write.py`
- **purpose:** `upstream/**` is read-only except `upstream/<tree>/_PATCHES/`. Each `station.yml: live_surfaces` glob is
  read-only except `<surface>/patches/`, whose files must open with `NOT APPLIED`.
- **implements:** LL-08, LL-18
- **acceptance:** both selftests exit 0. A redirect into `upstream/x/a.py` gives 2. A Write to
  `upstream/x/_PATCHES/p.md` whose first line is `NOT APPLIED` gives 0. A Read anywhere gives 0.

### CA-10 · hooks/deny_connector.py
- **kind:** hook (PreToolUse·`mcp__.*`, DENY)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/deny_connector.py`
- **purpose:** deny any `mcp__<server>__*` call whose server is not in `station.yml: connectors_allow`. This is the
  noun boundary enforced: client ERP data is reachable only from the BI station.
- **implements:** LL-04
- **acceptance:** the selftest exits 0, with an allowed server giving 0 and a disallowed server giving 2.
  `station_audit -k hooks_wired` confirms the hook is wired.

### CA-11 · hooks/context_ladder.py
- **kind:** hook (SessionStart `startup|resume|compact|clear`, REPORT)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/context_ladder.py`
- **purpose:** print the plan head, the newest checkpoint's `NEXT` block, `station_audit.py --state` and the open lanes,
  each within the per-source byte budget from `station.yml`.
- **implements:** LL-44, LL-13, LL-21
- **acceptance:** `python3 .claude/hooks/context_ladder.py --selftest` exits 0. Output on every source is no more than
  its budget and under 10,000 chars, and the `NEXT` block appears before anything else when the budget is tight.

### CA-12 · hooks/stop_twice.py
- **kind:** hook (PostToolUseFailure/TaskStop recorder plus PreToolUse·Bash deny)
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/stop_twice.py`
- **purpose:** a target that stopped twice in 24 h in one session is denied a third launch. Release is a `.released`
  file, a `RELEASES.yml` row, or 24 h.
- **implements:** LL-15, LL-14, LL-16
- **acceptance:** the selftest exits 0. Two planted stops followed by a third launch give 2. A `.released` file after
  that gives 0. Another session's stops do not count (0).

### CA-13 · hooks/worktree_state.py, hooks/remind_prior_art.py, hooks/deny_noted_defect.py and hooks/summon_cap_guard.py
- **kind:** hooks: Stop/SubagentStop REPORT, PreToolUse·Write REPORT, PreToolUse·Bash DENY on commit, and
  PreToolUse·Agent|Workflow DENY
- **path:** `.claude/hooks/*.py`
- **purpose:**
  - `worktree_state`: report a stale beat, a dirty worktree, or uncommitted work older than one cadence.
  - `remind_prior_art`: report on the creation of a new tool or skill.
  - `deny_noted_defect`: deny staged hedge-words with no register id.
  - `summon_cap_guard`: enforce `block_max_agents` within the window.
- **implements:** LL-37, LL-42, LL-06, LL-31, LL-34
- **acceptance:** each `--selftest` exits 0. `station_audit -k hook_channels` confirms the two Stop/Write REPORT hooks
  route through `_report.py`.

### CA-14 · tools/station_audit.py
- **kind:** script (stdlib plus PyYAML), one exit code
- **path:** `tools/station_audit.py`
- **purpose:** the station's claim checker, with `--state`, `--changed`, `-k`, `--gate`, an `UNREADABLE` sentinel,
  named filtered greens, denominator headlines and a trend file. Checks:

  | check | class | fails when |
  |---|---|---|
  | `station_yml` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | schema invalid |
  | `claudemd_bytes` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | CLAUDE.md over `bytes_budget` |
  | `rule_paths_resolve` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a `.claude/rules/*.md` `paths:` glob matches no tracked file |
  | `listing_budget` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | listed skills' name+description bytes over `listing_budget_bytes` |
  | `listing_overrides` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a routed workflow or verb with no override row; an override naming nothing or shadowing a skill |
  | `vendor_leak` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | any `upstream/**/.claude/{skills,agents,commands,settings*.json}`, `.mcp.json` or `.claude-plugin/` not renamed; a station instruction file quoting upstream agent text |
  | `upstream_index` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a tree undocumented in USAGE.yml, an `entry:` unresolved, a LICENSE missing |
  | `licence_filter` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a GPL/AGPL tree under `upstream/` in a proprietary station |
  | `precedence` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a tree missing from PRECEDENCE.yml, or `governs:` naming a NEVER concern |
  | `router_targets` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a `first_move` naming a missing workflow or skill; router selftest red |
  | `workflows_parse` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a saved workflow that does not parse (`node --check`) or has no certain test |
  | `certain_tests` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a certain test that is existence-only, cannot run, names no tool, or mutates |
  | `generated_fresh` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a re-render differs from the committed file |
  | `hooks_selftest` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | any hook `--selftest` non-zero |
  | `hooks_wired` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a wired script missing, or a hook script wired nowhere |
  | `hook_channels` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a report on a non-delivering event bypasses `_report`; a SessionStart reader without a budget |
  | `canon` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a duplicated un-pointered rule body; a drifted CANON block |
  | `ledger` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a duplicate id, a missing `hook:`, an empty or "be careful" amendment |
  | `checkpoints` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | a number without a command; a cited hash that does not resolve |
  | `paths` | MUST_BE_CLEAN | any path named in station.yml, CODEOWNERS, router, rules or USAGE fails to resolve |
  | `admission` | WORKLIST | a check or hook without `earned-by` / `selftest` / `class` / `retires` |
  | `hook_release` | WORKLIST | a deny hook without a `release:` line |
  | `handoff` | WORKLIST | a header field missing, a line-number anchor, a transcribed counter |
  | `anchors` | WORKLIST | `path.ext:NNN` in a durable doc |
  | `triggers` | WORKLIST | prints the distance to each parked trigger |
  | `cli_doc` | WORKLIST | an argparse flag absent from the docstring |

- **implements:** LL-01, LL-02, LL-03, LL-07, LL-08, LL-09, LL-10, LL-11, LL-13, LL-14, LL-19, LL-21, LL-22, LL-23,
  LL-24, LL-25, LL-29, LL-30, LL-33, LL-46, LL-47, LL-50
- **acceptance:** `python3 tools/station_audit.py --selftest` exits 0. It plants one defect per MUST_BE_CLEAN check in
  a `mktemp -d` fixture station and asserts that each check fails alone. It then asserts that a clean fixture is all
  green, that a `-k` run prints "N/M … the rest were NOT run", and that a scraper fed garbage returns UNREADABLE.

### CA-15 · Skills: summon-lite, tier-lite, handoff-lite, checkpoint, closeout
- **kind:** skills (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`); listed, because the model must choose to run them
- **path:** `.claude/skills/{summon,tier,handoff,checkpoint,closeout}/SKILL.md`

  - **checkpoint:** commit hash, paths, numbers with commands, owed with triggers, the next contract.

### CA-16 · upstream/USAGE.yml, upstream/PRECEDENCE.yml and tools/ingest_upstream.py

### CA-17 · Workflow skeleton with a live gather and a certain-test stage
- **kind:** workflow template (JS)
- **path:** `.claude/workflows/_template.js`
- **purpose:** stage 1 GATHER runs commands and injects their real output and exit codes, never prose. The last stage

### CA-18 · .station/ runtime directory convention
- **kind:** convention plus `.gitignore` rows
- **path:** `.station/{beats,pause,cache,returns}/`

### CA-19 · Domain packs (opt-in)
- **kind:** templates
- **path:** `commons/packs/trading/` (MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT.md, PREREGISTRATIONS.md, NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md, FIT-lens
  checklist) and `commons/packs/research/` (NEGATIVE_RESULTS.md and source-hop order)
- **purpose:** give the trading and research stations their domain discipline as opt-in files, so no non-trading
  station carries trading rules on its hot path. No BI pack is shipped, because no BI rule is derived here (see gaps).
- **implements:** LL-D1, LL-D2, LL-D3
- **acceptance:** the pack installs with `python3 tools/station_audit.py -k ledger -k paths` green, and the router gains
  the pack's intents with `router_targets` green.
